SCIENCE PASSAGE 7: Battery Voltage at Different Temperatures
Students placed identical batteries in temperature-controlled chambers for 30 minutes. They then connected each battery to the same resistor and recorded voltage immediately and after 5 minutes. Each temperature condition used a new battery from the same package.

According to the figure, what value was recorded for Initial voltage at the x-axis value 10?
A) 1.52
B) 1.53
C) 1.54
D) 1.38

SCIENCE PASSAGE 2: Mulch and Soil Infiltration
Students packed identical soil columns and applied simulated rain. Experiment 1 compared bare soil with 2 cm and 5 cm layers of straw mulch. They measured water collected below each column after 20 minutes. Experiment 2 repeated the treatments after gently compacting the soil.

According to the figure, what value was recorded for Uncompacted soil at the x-axis value 2?
F) 109
G) 74
H) 126
J) 83

questions.stem:
SCIENCE PASSAGE 6: How Migrating Birds Recalibrate Direction
Three students discuss how migrating birds correct their direction after several cloudy days.

Student 1: Birds rely mainly on the position of the setting sun. A clear sunset after cloudy weather allows them to reset an internal compass for the next day.

Student 2: Birds rely mainly on Earth’s magnetic field. Cloud cover has little effect on the compass itself; errors arise when local magnetic conditions are disturbed.

Student 3: Birds use both cues. Magnetic information provides a continuous reference, while sunset information can recalibrate how that magnetic reference is interpreted at a particular location.

Which prediction is most consistent with Student 3?
A) Changing either relevant factor could never affect the observation.
B) Student 3 predicts that changing the apparent sunset direction could alter later orientation even when magnetic cues remain available.
C) Only a factor that no student mentions could matter.
D) The phenomenon should remain perfectly constant over unlimited time.

options.A: Changing either relevant factor could never affect the observation.
options.B: Student 3 predicts that changing the apparent sunset direction could alter later orientation even when magnetic cues remain available.
options.C: Only a factor that no student mentions could matter.
options.D: The phenomenon should remain perfectly constant over unlimited time.

questions.explanation: The prediction follows from Student 3’s combined-mechanism explanation.

questions.stem:
SCIENCE PASSAGE 7: Pendulum Period, Length, and Mass
Students timed 10 swings of pendulums with two bob masses at several string lengths and divided by 10 to obtain period. The release angle was kept small and constant.

Which series had the greater value at 100?
F) 50 g bob
G) The values were exactly equal.
H) 100 g bob
J) The figure does not contain values for that condition.

options.C: 100 g bob
options.D: The figure does not contain values for that condition.

questions.explanation: Compare the two plotted values at the final x-position.

SCIENCE MATERIAL SET 7
Students tested how water temperature affected the time required for a tablet to dissolve. They used identical tablets, 106 mL of water in each cup, and stirred each cup at the same rate.

TABLE 1
Temperature (°C) | Dissolving time (s)
10 | 30
20 | 22
30 | 17
40 | 13

Trial 2 repeated the procedure with twice the water volume. Researcher 1 claims that higher temperature increases particle motion and therefore decreases dissolving time. Researcher 2 agrees that temperature matters but claims that stirring rate is the dominant factor whenever stirring is not controlled.

If the trend continues, a 45°C trial would most likely have a dissolving time:
A) greater than 30 seconds
B) exactly the 10°C time
C) that cannot be compared with any listed time
D) less than 13 seconds

options.C: that cannot be compared with any listed time
options.D: less than 13 seconds
